test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

What the council could not anticipate (1)/ was that the regulatory changes, sudden as they seemed, (2)/ were in fact a culmination of several years (3)/ of there being dissatisfaction within the sector. (4)
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option (4)**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**there being dissatisfaction**" is grammatically awkward and incorrect in this context.
 
• After the phrase "**a culmination of several years**", a noun phrase such as "**years of dissatisfaction**" or "**years of growing dissatisfaction**" should be used.
 
• Thus, the error lies in **Part (4)**.
 
• **Parts (1), (2), and (3)** are grammatically correct and logically connected.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"What the council could not anticipate was that the regulatory changes, sudden as they seemed, were in fact a culmination of several years of **growing dissatisfaction**__ within the sector."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The expression "**there being**" is sometimes used in absolute constructions, but it is not suitable here after "a culmination of several years".
 
• A concise noun phrase improves both grammar and clarity.
